arxiv-2104-09910.title: Interacting Brownian particles exhibiting enhanced rectification in an asymmetric channel
arxiv-2104-09910.creator: Narender Khatri, P. S. Burada
arxiv-2104-09910.description: Abstract Rectification of interacting Brownian particles is investigated in a two-dimensional asymmetric channel in the presence of an external periodic driving force. The periodic driving force can break the thermodynamic equilibrium and induces rectification of particles (or finite average velocity). The spatial variation in the shape of the channel leads to entropic barriers, which indeed control the rectification of particles.

arxiv-2110-08288.title: Explaining deep learning of galaxy morphology with saliency mapping 2021 Explaining deep learning of galaxy morphology with saliency mapping – 7
arxiv-2110-08288.creator: Prabh Bhambra, Benjamin Joachimi, Ofer Lahav
arxiv-2110-08288.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Prabh Bhambra, Benjamin Joachimi, Ofer Lahav. We successfully demonstrate the use of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques on astronomical datasets in the context of measuring galactic bar lengths. The method consists of training convolutional neural networks on human classified data from Galaxy Zoo in order to predict general galaxy morphologies, and then using SmoothGrad (a saliency mapping technique) to extract the bar for measurement by a bespoke algorithm.

arxiv-2205-10266.title: Analysis of Co-Laughter Gesture Relationship on RGB videos in Dyadic Conversation Context
arxiv-2205-10266.description: Abstract The development of virtual agents has enabled human-avatar interactions to become increasingly rich and varied. Moreover, an expressive virtual agent i.e. that mimics the natural expression of emotions, enhances social interaction between a user (human) and an agent (intelligent machine).

arxiv-2210-08247.title: A sparse spectral method for fractional differential equations in one-spatial dimension
arxiv-2210-08247.creator: Ioannis P. A. Papadopoulos, Sheehan Olver
arxiv-2210-08247.description: Abstract We develop a sparse spectral method for a class of fractional differential equations, posed on ℝ \mathbb{R} , in one dimension. These equations may include sqrt-Laplacian, Hilbert, derivative, and identity terms. The numerical method utilizes a basis consisting of weighted Chebyshev polynomials of the second kind in conjunction with their Hilbert transforms.

arxiv-2311-09129.title: A short note on effective Pauli noise models
arxiv-2311-09129.creator: Michael A. Perlin
arxiv-2311-09129.description: Abstract We provide a simple prescription to extract an effective Pauli noise model from classical simulations of a noisy experimental protocol for a unitary gate. This prescription yields the closest Pauli channel approximation to the error channel associated with the gate implementation, as measured by the Frobenius distance between quantum channels.

arxiv-2504-06748.title: Efficient Deployment of Spiking Neural Networks on SpiNNaker2 for DVS Gesture Recognition Using Neuromorphic Intermediate Representation
arxiv-2504-06748.creator: Sirine Arfa 1 2 , Bernhard Vogginger 1 , Chen Liu 1 , Johannes Partzsch 1 , Mark Schöne 1 Christian Mayr 1 6 4
arxiv-2504-06748.description: Abstract Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) are highly energy-efficient during inference, making them particularly suitable for deployment on neuromorphic hardware. Their ability to process event-driven inputs, such as data from dynamic vision sensors (DVS), further enhances their applicability to edge computing tasks.

arxiv-2510-22006.title: Linking congruences for PED and POD partitions
arxiv-2510-22006.creator: Dalen Dockery, Marie Jameson
arxiv-2510-22006.description: Abstract . Recent work of Garvan, Sellers, Smoot, and others has made connections between infinite families of congruences for various partition functions. Here, we apply this approach to families of congruences for PED and POD partitions and find that they are naturally linked to congruence families for overpartitions into odd parts and overpartitions. 1.

arxiv-2512-06600.title: Learning Reachability of Energy Storage Arbitrage
arxiv-2512-06600.creator: Tomás Tapia, Agustin Castellano, Enrique Mallada, Yury Dvorkin
arxiv-2512-06600.description: Abstract Power systems face increasing weather-driven variability and, therefore, increasingly rely on flexible but energy-limited storage resources. Energy storage can buffer this variability, but its value depends on intertemporal decisions under uncertain prices. Without accounting for the future reliability value of stored energy, batteries may act myopically, discharging too early or failing to preserve reserves during critical hours.

pmc-10754530.title: Stilbenes: a promising small molecule modulator for epigenetic regulation in human diseases
pmc-10754530.creator: Jing Tian, Li Jin, Hongquan Liu, Zichun Hua
pmc-10754530.description: Stilbenes are characterized by a vinyl group connecting two benzene rings to form the basic parent nucleus. pmc-13008825.title: Integrating Lab‐ and Field‐Based Approaches to Decipher Individuals' Response to Anthropogenic Change
pmc-13008825.creator: M. de Guinea, R. Landesman, J. R. Madden, T. Bugnyar, Y. Bartan, R. Nathan
pmc-13008825.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The global expansion of human activities increasingly exposes wild animals to novel, potentially threatening conditions. Consistent behavioural responses to perceived risk may be detrimental to wildlife, either by limiting foraging opportunities or by overexposing them to lethal hazards. We examine the relationship between risk responses, movement patterns and survival in fan‐tailed ravens ( Corvus rhipidurus ) inhabiting Israel's Dead Sea coastline.

pmc-13209558.title: Response Surface Analysis of Thermo-Hydraulic Performance of a Direct Absorption Solar Receiver Using Fe3O4 Nanofluid Under Concentrated Solar Irradiation
pmc-13209558.creator: Jeonggyun Ham, Hyemin Kim, Sang-Bum Ryu, Honghyun Cho
pmc-13209558.description: This study investigates the thermo-hydraulic performance of a spiral-channel direct absorption solar collector (DASC) using Response Surface Methodology (RSM). The objective of this study was to establish a design framework that balances thermal efficiency (ηth) and pressure drop (ΔP) by resolving inherent trade-offs. The results indicate that geometric parameters primarily influence hydraulic resistance, while optical factors govern thermal capture.
